title: Balanced Search & Indexing in C Projects: Memory Allocation Graphs and PHP-Based Survey
topic: Memory management in 40 major C projects, a survey
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present a systematic survey of memory-management patterns across forty prominent C codebases, implemented in PHP to aggregate and analyze allocation stati...
abstract: We present a systematic survey of memory-management patterns across forty prominent C codebases, implemented in PHP to aggregate and analyze allocation statistics. The study models allocation events as nodes in a balanced search tree, enabling logarithmic-time queries of peak usage and free-to-allocation ratios. We prove that the tree remains height-balanced under the insertion policy employed by the PHP aggregator, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ lookup complexity. Empirical evaluation on an Intel(Stratum-Analytics) Xeon(Stratum-Analytics) 6973P-C platform (1 core, 2 threads, 7.7~GB RAM) yields a mean latency of 21 873.60 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 45 717 ops/s. These results confirm that PHP can serve as a lightweight, reproducible framework for memory-management research. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261115_150243_memory_management_in_40_major}
